text:
Alicia M.: Quick heads-up — noticed a perf regression on small-batch chat workloads after yesterday's runtime patch. nsight capture attached (run1.nsys).
Tom R.: ack, saw the alert. rough numbers?
Alicia M.: baseline (before patch) median token lat = 48ms, after patch = 78ms on p4d. ~60% of extra time is in the bwd path of matmul kernels + allocator stalls.
Vincent: allocation stalls? like cudaMalloc/free bouncing?
Alicia M.: yeah, nsys timeline shows repeated ~100-250ms CPU blocks labeled cudaMalloc in between GPU kernels. GPU sits idle then we fallback to a different cuBLASLt algo.
profiler-bot: nsys summary: cublasLt heuristics picked algo id=7 which needs 2.1MB workspace, successful -> 420us per GEMM. fallback path (algo id=0 naive) -> 860us per GEMM. Workspace alloc attempts: 73, failed_allocs: 19, total cudaMalloc time: 1.3s.
Priya: do we have the trace snippet?
Alicia M.: pasted timeline extract:
```
CPU: 12:34:57.120 cudaMalloc 180ms
GPU: 12:34:57.305 cublasLtGemm algo=7 start -> 420us
CPU: 12:34:57.306 cudaFree 40ms
CPU: 12:34:57.350 cudaMalloc 210ms (failed then fallback)
GPU: 12:34:57.563 fallback_sgemm start -> 860us
```
Jay: Very weird — why would cudaMalloc be that expensive mid-run? we've been pooling for the long-lived tensors. Did the patch touch allocator fallback paths?
Tom R.: the runtime patch swapped to a stricter page-alignment policy (reduce fragmentation) but apparently it causes more granular allocations for temporary workspaces. allocator logs show small arenas being torn down between requests.
Vincent: That would explain fragmentation spikes then subsequent slow cudaMalloc calls while defrag runs. cuBLASLt probes workspace size, then we call cudaMalloc for workspace. If it fails we trigger cublasLt with algo that uses no workspace or smaller buf.
Priya: Can we force the algorithm selection to ignore heuristics and choose a fixed algo for the suspect shapes to reproduce?
Alicia M.: yes, I ran a quick sweep with env var CUBLASLT_ALGO_OVERRIDE=7 and the latency goes back to ~50ms but we still see intermittent cudaMalloc stalls (because override doesn't avoid alloc).
Jay: Hmm. two separate issues: 1) allocator churn causing cudaMalloc spikes 2) cuBLASLt heuristic falling back when alloc fails -> slower path. We should address (1) first.
Tom R.: proposed short-term mitigation: pre-allocate a workspace pool per device for commonly probed sizes (1MB, 2MB, 4MB) and hand out from pool instead of calling malloc. cheap and low-risk.
Priya: agree. Also add a cublasLt probe cache keyed by (shape, dtype, device, batch_size) so we avoid repeated heuristic calls that trigger allocs.
Vincent: for reproducing locally: nsys capture command I used:
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/run1 --trace=cuda,cublas,cudnn --sample=none --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --sleep=0.1 --force-overwrite --similarity 0.1 ./inference_binary --batch 4 --seq 128
```
Alicia M.: attaching raw perf numbers from the run: total tokens=10000, time_before_patch=12.1s, time_after_patch=19.5s; slow kernels: gemm_fwd (420us->860us when fallback), allocator cumulative 1.3s.
ops-bot: FYI created ticket RNW-2318 for allocator pool + probe cache. assigned to Tom R. and Priya. SLA: P2.
Jay: experiments to run: 1) enable pooling + perf sweep 2) run batch sweep (1,2,4,8) to see batching heuristic interaction 3) run cublasLt algo override matrix to check quality/regression; collect nsys for each.
Tom R.: I'll drop a small patch with a pooled workspace allocator behind a feature flag. want quick perf run Friday AM.
Vincent: one more thought — double-check stream synchronization. I saw in perfetto correlations where host waits for a cudaEvent right before allocating. maybe we can overlap alloc with CPU-side work to hide latency.
Priya: good call. I'll add probe cache and an opt-in override for probe frequency (only probe once per cold start).
Alicia M.: thanks. leaving the nsys capture in the thread: run1.nsys, perfetto link: https://perfetto.prod/runs/1855/abc123. ping me if you need the binary or repro harness. :thumbsup:
Tom R.: thanks team, I'll iterate on the pool and post results here.
Jay: mark as follow-up for mid-week perf review. :eyes:
